angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 561,430 km at 137.68 pc = 0.05 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 7.2630 +/- 0.0156 mas (same row, RUWE 1.17): 137.68 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.807 +/- 0.016 solar radii from Livingston et al. 2019, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of K2-53 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2019AJ....157..102L/abstract): 561,430 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.851 +/- 0.032 solar masses from Livingston et al. 2019, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of K2-53 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2019AJ....157..102L/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 5263 +/- 88 K from Livingston et al. 2019, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of K2-53 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2019AJ....157..102L/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Livingston et al. 2019, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of K2-53 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2019AJ....157..102L/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/k2-53.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.554, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, coloured from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
